The man from the Muhajireen gained the upper hand over al-Buhaiz, so al-Buhaiz said: O group of Ansar, so some men from the Ansar supported him. The Muhajireen said: O group of Muhajireen, so some men from the Muhajireen supported him until there was some fighting between those men from the Muhajireen and the men from the Ansar, then a barrier was established between them, and every hypocrite or man in whose heart there was sickness withdrew to Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul, who said: You had hoped and been repelled, but now you are neither harming nor… It is useful, the jalabiyas have joined forces against us and they were calling every hadith of the migration jalabiyas, so Abdullah bin Ubayy, the enemy of God, said: By God, if we return to Medina, the more honorable will expel the more humiliated from it. Malik ibn Ad-Dukhshan, who was one of the hypocrites, said: Did I not tell you not to spend on those who are with the Messenger of God until they disperse? Umar ibn Al-Khattab heard of that, so he walked until he came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: O Messenger of God, give me permission to strike off this man who has led people astray. He meant Umar Abdullah ibn Ubayy. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to Umar: Or will you fight him if I order you to kill him? Umar said: Yes, by God, if you order me to kill him, I will strike off his head. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Sit down. Then Asid ibn Hudayr, who was one of the Ansar and then one of Banu Abd Al-Ashhal, came until he came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: O Messenger of God, give me permission to strike off this man who has led people astray. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Or will you fight him if I order you to kill him? He said: Yes, by God, if you order me to kill him, I will strike with the sword under his earring. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Sit down. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Give permission to depart. So he set out with the people and traveled that day, night, and the next day until the day was over. Then he dismounted and set out with the people for the same amount of time until he arrived in Medina in the morning, in three days, which he traveled from the back of the paralyzed. When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) arrived in Medina, he sent for Umar and summoned him. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to him, Which Umar would you have killed if I had ordered you to kill him? Umar said, Yes. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, “By God, if I had killed him that day, I would have humiliated men who, if I ordered them today to kill him, would have obeyed, and people would say that I attacked my companions and killed them patiently.” Then God, the Almighty, revealed, “They are the ones who say, ‘Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of God until they disperse.’ But to God belong the treasures of the heavens and the earth, but the hypocrites do not understand. They say, ‘If we return to Medina,’” 10:17. This is a strange context and it contains precious things that are not found anywhere else. Muhammad bin Ishaq bin Yasar said: Asim bin Omar bin Qatada told me that when Abdullah bin Abdullah bin Ubayy heard what had happened to his father, he came to the Messenger of God and said: O Messenger of God, I have heard that you want to kill Abdullah bin Ubayy because of what you have heard about him. If you are going to do it, then order me to do it and I will bring you his head. By God, the Khazraj know that they have never had a man more dutiful to his father than me. I fear that you will order someone other than me to kill him, but my soul will not allow me to see the killer of Abdullah bin Ubayy walking among the people and I kill him, thus killing a believer for an unbeliever and entering Hell. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Rather, we will be gentle with him and treat him well as long as he remains with us. Ikrimah, Ibn Zayd and others mentioned that when the people returned to Madinah, Abdullah ibn Abdullah stood at the gate of Madinah and drew his sword. People started passing by him. When his father, Abdullah ibn Ubayy, came, his son said to him: Behind you! He said: What is wrong with you, woe to you? He said: “By God, you will not pass from here until the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gives you permission, for he is the powerful one and you are the weak one.” When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came, and he was only walking in the rear, Abdullah ibn Ubayy complained to him about his son. His son Abdullah said: By God, O Messenger of God, he will not enter it until you give him permission. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave him permission. Abdullah said: “Now that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, has given you permission, then pass now.” Abu Bakr Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr Al-Hamidi said in his Musnad: Sufyan bin Uyaynah told us, Abu Harun Al-Madani told us: Abdullah bin Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul said to his father: By God, you will never enter Madinah until you say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is the most honorable and I am the most humiliated. He said: He came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, I have heard that you want to kill my father. By Him who sent you with the truth, I have never looked at his face out of awe of him. If you wish me to bring you his head, I will come to you, for I hate to see my father’s killer.
63:7: God the Almighty says, informing us about the hypocrites, upon whom be the curses of God, that And when it is said to them, ‘Come, that the Messenger of God may ask forgiveness for you,’ they turn their heads away, meaning they turn away and turn away from what is said to them out of arrogance and contempt for what is said to them. For this reason God the Almighty said: And you see them turning away while they are arrogant. Then He punished them for that, saying: “It is the same for them whether you ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them. God will never forgive them. Indeed, God does not guide the defiantly disobedient people,” as He said in Surat Bara’ah. We have already discussed that and cited the hadiths narrated there. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ibn Abi Omar Al-Adani told us: Sufyan said, They turned their heads. Ibn Abi Omar said: Sufyan turned his face to his right and looked askance, then said, This is him. More than one of the early Muslims mentioned that this entire chain of narration was revealed regarding Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul, as we will mention soon, God willing. He is trustworthy and upon him we rely. Muhammad bin Ishaq said in the biography: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to Medina, meaning his return from Uhud, Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul, as Ibn Shihab al-Zuhri told me, had a position that he would stand at every Friday. He would not deny the honor he had in himself and his people, and he was honorable among them. When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sat on a Friday while delivering a sermon to the people, he would stand and say: O people, this is the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, among you. God has honored you through him and made you strong through him, so support him, honor him, listen to him, and obey him. Then he would sit until he did what he did on the day of Uhud, meaning his return with a third of the army and the people had returned. He stood and did that as he used to do. The Muslims took hold of his clothes from the sides and said: Sit down, enemy of God, you are not worthy of that, having done what you did. So he went out, stepping over people’s necks, saying: By God, it is as if I had spoken a lie. If I stood up, I would intensify his matter. Some men from the Ansar met him at the door of the mosque and said: Woe to you, what is the matter with you? He said: I stood up to try to tighten his grip, but some of his companions jumped on me, pulling me and scolding me. It was as if I had said, I am going to tighten my grip. They said: Woe to you! Go back so that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) may ask forgiveness for you. He said: By God, I do not want him to ask forgiveness for me. Qatada and As-Suddi said: This verse was revealed about Abdullah ibn Ubayy. A young man from his relatives went to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and told him a hadith about him and a serious matter. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) called him and he swore by God and disavowed that. The Ansar turned to that young man and blamed him and removed him. God revealed about him what you hear. It was said to the enemy of God: Why don’t you go to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him)? He began to shake his head, meaning you will not do it. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abu Al-Rabi’ Al-Zahrani told us, Hammad ibn Zayd told us, Ayoub told us on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr that whenever the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) stopped at a place, he would not leave until he prayed there. When the Battle of Tabuk took place, he heard that Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul had said: The more honorable will expel the more humble from it. So he left before stopping at the end of the day. It was said to Abdul God ibn Ubayy said: Go to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) so that he may seek forgiveness for you. So God revealed: “When the hypocrites come to you, they say, ‘We bear witness that you are the Messenger of God.’ And God knows that you are His Messenger, and God bears witness that the hypocrites are liars. They have taken their oaths as a shield and averted [people] from the way of God. Evil indeed is that which they have been doing. That is because they believed and then disbelieved, so their hearts were sealed, so they do not understand. And when you see them, their bodies impress you, and when they speak, you listen to their speech. They are as if they were propped up pieces of wood. They think that every shout is against them. They are the enemy, so beware of them. May God destroy them! How are they deluded? And when it is said to them, ‘Come, that the Messenger of God may ask forgiveness for you,’ they turn their heads away.” This is a sound chain of transmission going back to Sa’id ibn Jubayr. His statement that this was during the Battle of Tabuk is questionable, rather it is not good, because Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul was not among those who went out on the Battle of Tabuk, but rather he returned with a group of the army. Rather, what is well-known among the authors of military expeditions and biographies is that this was during the Battle of Al-Murays’i’, which is the Battle of Banu Al-Mustaliq. Yunus bin Bakir said on the authority of Ibn Ishaq: Muhammad bin Yahya bin Hibban, Abdullah bin Abi Bakr, and Asim bin Umar bin Qatada told me in the story of Banu al-Mustaliq, that while the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was staying there, Jahjah bin Saeed al-Ghifari, who was a servant of Umar bin al-Khattab, and Sinan bin Wabar fought over water. Ibn Ishaq said: Muhammad bin Yahya bin Hibban told me: They crowded together over water and fought. Sinan said: O group of Ansar, and Jahjah said: O group of Muhajireen, and Zaid bin Arqam and a group of Ansar were with Abdullah bin Ubayy, and when he heard it he said: They have revolted against us in our country, and by God, we and these Quraysh robes are nothing but what the one who said: Fatten your dog and it will eat you, and by God, if we return to Medina, the more honorable will expel from it the more abject. Then he turned to those of his people who were with him and said: What have you done to yourselves? You have made them your country and shared your wealth with them. By God, if you had refrained from… Zaid bin Arqam may God be pleased with him heard it and went with it to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) while he was a young boy in the household of Umar bin Al-Khattab may God be pleased with him and told him the story. Umar may God be pleased with him said: O Messenger of God, order Ibad bin Bishr to have his head struck off. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: What will happen when people say, O Umar, that Muhammad kills his companions? No, but call out, O Umar, to leave. When Abdullah bin Ubayy heard that this had reached the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), he came to him and apologized to him, and swore by God that he had not said what Zaid bin Arqam had said. He was in a good place with his people and they said: O Messenger of God, perhaps this young boy was mistaken and what the man said was not proven. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) set out during a time when he usually did not set out. He was met by Usaid ibn Hudayr may God be pleased with him. He greeted him with the greeting of the Prophet and then said: By God, you have set out at a strange time when you do not usually set out. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Have you not heard what your companion Ibn Ubayy said? He claimed that when he comes to Madinah, the more honorable will expel from it the more humble. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: So you, O Messenger of God, are the honorable one and he is the humble one. Then he said: Be gentle with him, O Messenger of God, for by God, God brought you while we were stringing beads for him to go out, and he thinks that you have taken away his kingdom. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) set out with the people until evening, and the whole night until morning, and the beginning of the day until the sun had risen. Then he descended with the people to distract them from what he was talking about. The people were not safe from feeling the touch of the ground, so they slept, and Surah Al-Munafiqun was revealed. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bayhaqi said: Abu Abdullah Al-Hafiz told us, Abu Bakr bin Ishaq told us, Bishr bin Musa told us, Al-Hamidi told us, Sufyan told us, Umar bin Dinar told us, I heard Jabir bin Abdullah say: We were with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in a military campaign, and a man from the Muhajireen kicked a man from the Ansar. The Ansari said: O Ansar! And the Muhajireen said: O Muhajireen! So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: What is this call to ignorance? Leave it, for it is rotten. Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul said: They did it, and by God, if we return to Medina, the more honorable will expel the more humiliated from it. Jabir said: The Ansar were more numerous in Medina than the Muhajireen when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, arrived, then the Muhajireen increased in number after that, so Umar said: Let me strike off the head of this hypocrite. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Leave him, lest people say that Muhammad kills his companions. Imam Ahmad narrated it on the authority of Husayn bin Muhammad al-Marwazi on the authority of Sufyan bin Uyaynah, and al-Bukhari narrated it on the authority of al-Hamidi and Muslim on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah and others on the authority of Sufyan with a similar chain of transmission. Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us, Shu`bah told us, on the authority of al-Hakam, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka`b al-Qurazi, on the authority of Zayd ibn Arqam, who said: I was with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, during the Battle of Tabuk, and Abdullah ibn Ubayy said: If we return to Medina, the more honorable will expel the more humble from it. He said: So I came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and informed him. He said: Abdullah ibn Ubayy swore that none of that had happened. He said: My people blamed me and said: What did you want with this? He said: So I went and slept gloomy and sad. He said: Then the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent for me and said: God has accepted your excuse and confirmed your truth. He said: Then this verse was revealed: “They are the ones who say, ‘Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of God until they disperse.’ And to God belong the treasures of the heavens and the earth, but the hypocrites do not understand. They say, ‘If we return to Medina, the more honorable will surely expel therefrom the more humble.’” Al-Bukhari narrated it at this verse on the authority of Adam bin Abi Iyas on the authority of Shu’bah, then he said: Ibn Abi Za’idah said on the authority of Al-A’mash on the authority of Amr on the authority of Ibn Abi Layla on the authority of Zayd on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Tirmidhi and Al-Nasa’i also narrated it at this verse on the authority of Shu’bah on his authority. Another chain of transmission on the authority of Zayd Imam Ahmad, may God have mercy on him, said: Yahya bin Adam and Yahya bin Abi Bakir told us: Israel told us on the authority of Abu Ishaq, who said: I heard Zayd bin Arqam, and Ibn Abi Bakir said on the authority of Zayd bin Arqam, who said: I went out with my uncle on a military expedition and I heard Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul saying to his companions: Do not spend on those with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and if we return to Madinah, the more honorable will expel the more humble from it. So I mentioned that to my uncle, and my uncle mentioned it to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent for me, and I told him. So he sent for Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul and his companions, and they swore by God that they had not said anything. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called me a liar and he believed him, and I was afflicted with a worry the like of which I had never been afflicted with before. I sat in the house, and my uncle said: I only wanted the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to call you a liar and hate you! He said: Until God revealed, When the hypocrites come to you, He said: So the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) sent for me and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) recited it to me and then said: God has confirmed what you say. Then Ahmad also said: Hasan bin Musa told us, Zuhair told us, Abu Ishaq told us that he heard Zaid bin Arqam say: We went out with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) on a journey and hardship befell the people. Abdullah bin Ubayy said to his companions: Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) until they disperse from around him. He said: If we return to Madinah, the more honorable will expel therefrom the more humble. So I came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and informed him of that. He sent for Abdullah bin Ubayy and asked him, and he swore an oath as to what he should do. They said: Zaid lied, O Messenger of God. I was impressed by what they said, so God revealed my confirmation, When the hypocrites come to you, He said: And the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) called them and asked forgiveness for them, but they turned their heads. And the Almighty said: As if they were propped up pieces of wood. He said: They were men of the most beautiful kind. Al-Bukhari, Muslim, and Al-Nasa’i narrated it from the hadith of Zuhair. Al-Bukhari also narrated it, and Al-Tirmidhi from the hadith of Israel, both of them on the authority of Abu Ishaq Amr bin Abdullah Al-Subai’i Al-Hamadani Al-Kufi on the authority of Zaid with it. Another chain of transmission on the authority of Zayd Abu Isa al-Tirmidhi said: Abd ibn Humayd told us, Ubayd God ibn Musa told us, on the authority of Isra’il, on the authority of al-Suddi, on the authority of Abu Sa’id al-Azdi, who said: Zayd ibn Arqam told us: We went on an expedition with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and there were some Bedouins with us. We would race to the water, and the Bedouins would get to it before us. A Bedouin raced his companions to fill the basin, placing stones around it and putting a mat on it until his companions came. He said: Then a man from the Ansar came to the Bedouin and let go of the reins of his camel so that she could drink, but he refused to let go, so he grabbed a stone and the water subsided. The Bedouin raised his stick and struck the Ansari on the head with it, wounding him. Then Abdullah ibn Ubayy, the head of the hypocrites, came and informed him, and he was one of his companions. Abdullah ibn Ubayy became angry and said: Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of God until they disperse from around him, meaning the Bedouins. They used to attend the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he was eating. Then Abdullah said to his companions: When they disperse from Muhammad Bring Muhammad food so he and those with him can eat. Then he said to his companions: If you return to Medina, let the more honorable expel the more humble. Zaid said: I was riding behind my uncle. I heard Abdullah ibn Ubayy say what he said, so I informed my uncle. He went and informed the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) sent for him, and he swore an oath and denied it. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) believed him and called me a liar. My uncle came to me and said: I only wanted the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) to hate you and for the Muslims to call you a liar. I was overcome by such grief as had never befallen anyone before. While I was traveling with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) on a journey, and my head was heavy with worry, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came to me, stroked my ear, and smiled in my face. I would not have liked to have eternal life because of it. Then Abu Bakr caught up with me and said: What did the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say to you? I said: He did not say anything except that he stroked my ear and smiled in my face. He said: Be of good cheer. Then Umar caught up with me, and I said to him the same as I had said to Abu Bakr. When morning came, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) recited Surat al-Munafiqun. Al-Tirmidhi was the only one to transmit it and said: This is a good and authentic hadith. Al-Hafiz Al-Bayhaqi narrated it in this way on the authority of Al-Hakim on the authority of Abu Al-Abbas Muhammad ibn Ahmad Al-Mahboubi on the authority of Saeed ibn Masoud on the authority of Ubaidullah ibn Musa with it, and he added after the words of Surat al-Munafiqun 63:When the hypocrites come to you, they say, ‘We bear witness that you are the Messenger of God,’ until he reached They are the ones who say, ‘Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of God until they disperse,’ until he reached The more honorable will surely expel therefrom the more humble. Abdullah bin Lahi’ah narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Aswad Urwah bin Al-Zubayr in Al-Maghāzī, and Musa bin Uqbah also mentioned this story in this context in his Magāzī, but they made the one who conveyed the words of Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was Aws bin Arqam from Banu Al-Harith bin Al-Khazraj, so perhaps it was another conveyor or a misprint due to hearing, and God knows best. Ibn Abi Hatim, may God have mercy on him, said: Muhammad bin Aziz al-Ayli told us, Salamah told me, Aqil told me, Muhammad bin Muslim told me that Urwah bin al-Zubayr and Amr bin Thabit al-Ansari told him that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, led the expedition of al-Marisi’, in which the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, demolished the tyrant Manat, which was between the back of the paralyzed man and the sea. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent Khalid bin al-Walid, who defeated Manat. Two men fought in that expedition of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, one of them was from the Muhajireen and the other from Buhaiz, and they were allies of the Ansar. The man from the Muhajireen gained the upper hand over al-Buhaiz, so al-Buhaiz said: O group of Ansar, so some men from the Ansar supported him. The Muhajireen said: O group of Muhajireen, so some men from the Muhajireen supported him until there was some fighting between those men from the Muhajireen and the men from the Ansar, then a barrier was established between them, and every hypocrite or man in whose heart there was sickness withdrew to Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul, who said: You had hoped and been repelled, but now you are neither harming nor… It is useful, the jalabiyas have joined forces against us and they were calling every hadith of the migration jalabiyas, so Abdullah bin Ubayy, the enemy of God, said: By God, if we return to Medina, the more honorable will expel the more humiliated from it. Malik ibn Ad-Dukhshan, who was one of the hypocrites, said: Did I not tell you not to spend on those who are with the Messenger of God until they disperse? Umar ibn Al-Khattab heard of that, so he walked until he came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: O Messenger of God, give me permission to strike off this man who has led people astray. He meant Umar Abdullah ibn Ubayy. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to Umar: Or will you fight him if I order you to kill him? Umar said: Yes, by God, if you order me to kill him, I will strike off his head. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Sit down. Then Asid ibn Hudayr, who was one of the Ansar and then one of Banu Abd Al-Ashhal, came until he came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: O Messenger of God, give me permission to strike off this man who has led people astray. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Or will you fight him if I order you to kill him? He said: Yes, by God, if you order me to kill him, I will strike with the sword under his earring. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Sit down. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Give permission to depart. So he set out with the people and traveled that day, night, and the next day until the day was over. Then he dismounted and set out with the people for the same amount of time until he arrived in Medina in the morning, in three days, which he traveled from the back of the paralyzed. When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) arrived in Medina, he sent for Umar and summoned him. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to him, Which Umar would you have killed if I had ordered you to kill him? Umar said, Yes. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, “By God, if I had killed him that day, I would have humiliated men who, if I ordered them today to kill him, would have obeyed, and people would say that I attacked my companions and killed them patiently.” Then God, the Almighty, revealed, “They are the ones who say, ‘Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of God until they disperse.’ But to God belong the treasures of the heavens and the earth, but the hypocrites do not understand. They say, ‘If we return to Medina,’” 10:17. This is a strange context and it contains precious things that are not found anywhere else. Muhammad bin Ishaq bin Yasar said: Asim bin Omar bin Qatada told me that when Abdullah bin Abdullah bin Ubayy heard what had happened to his father, he came to the Messenger of God and said: O Messenger of God, I have heard that you want to kill Abdullah bin Ubayy because of what you have heard about him. If you are going to do it, then order me to do it and I will bring you his head. By God, the Khazraj know that they have never had a man more dutiful to his father than me. I fear that you will order someone other than me to kill him, but my soul will not allow me to see the killer of Abdullah bin Ubayy walking among the people and I kill him, thus killing a believer for an unbeliever and entering Hell. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Rather, we will be gentle with him and treat him well as long as he remains with us. Ikrimah, Ibn Zayd and others mentioned that when the people returned to Madinah, Abdullah ibn Abdullah stood at the gate of Madinah and drew his sword. People started passing by him. When his father, Abdullah ibn Ubayy, came, his son said to him: Behind you! He said: What is wrong with you, woe to you? He said: “By God, you will not pass from here until the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gives you permission, for he is the powerful one and you are the weak one.” When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came, and he was only walking in the rear, Abdullah ibn Ubayy complained to him about his son. His son Abdullah said: By God, O Messenger of God, he will not enter it until you give him permission. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave him permission. Abdullah said: “Now that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, has given you permission, then pass now.” Abu Bakr Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr Al-Hamidi said in his Musnad: Sufyan bin Uyaynah told us, Abu Harun Al-Madani told us: Abdullah bin Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul said to his father: By God, you will never enter Madinah until you say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is the most honorable and I am the most humiliated. He said: He came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, I have heard that you want to kill my father. By Him who sent you with the truth, I have never looked at his face out of awe of him. If you wish me to bring you his head, I will come to you, for I hate to see my father’s killer.
63:8: God the Almighty says, informing us about the hypocrites, upon whom be the curses of God, that And when it is said to them, ‘Come, that the Messenger of God may ask forgiveness for you,’ they turn their heads away, meaning they turn away and turn away from what is said to them out of arrogance and contempt for what is said to them. For this reason God the Almighty said: And you see them turning away while they are arrogant. Then He punished them for that, saying: “It is the same for them whether you ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them. God will never forgive them. Indeed, God does not guide the defiantly disobedient people,” as He said in Surat Bara’ah. We have already discussed that and cited the hadiths narrated there. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ibn Abi Omar Al-Adani told us: Sufyan said, They turned their heads. Ibn Abi Omar said: Sufyan turned his face to his right and looked askance, then said, This is him. More than one of the early Muslims mentioned that this entire chain of narration was revealed regarding Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul, as we will mention soon, God willing. He is trustworthy and upon him we rely. Muhammad bin Ishaq said in the biography: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to Medina, meaning his return from Uhud, Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul, as Ibn Shihab al-Zuhri told me, had a position that he would stand at every Friday. He would not deny the honor he had in himself and his people, and he was honorable among them. When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sat on a Friday while delivering a sermon to the people, he would stand and say: O people, this is the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, among you. God has honored you through him and made you strong through him, so support him, honor him, listen to him, and obey him. Then he would sit until he did what he did on the day of Uhud, meaning his return with a third of the army and the people had returned. He stood and did that as he used to do. The Muslims took hold of his clothes from the sides and said: Sit down, enemy of God, you are not worthy of that, having done what you did. So he went out, stepping over people’s necks, saying: By God, it is as if I had spoken a lie. If I stood up, I would intensify his matter. Some men from the Ansar met him at the door of the mosque and said: Woe to you, what is the matter with you? He said: I stood up to try to tighten his grip, but some of his companions jumped on me, pulling me and scolding me. It was as if I had said, I am going to tighten my grip. They said: Woe to you! Go back so that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) may ask forgiveness for you. He said: By God, I do not want him to ask forgiveness for me. Qatada and As-Suddi said: This verse was revealed about Abdullah ibn Ubayy. A young man from his relatives went to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and told him a hadith about him and a serious matter. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) called him and he swore by God and disavowed that. The Ansar turned to that young man and blamed him and removed him. God revealed about him what you hear. It was said to the enemy of God: Why don’t you go to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him)? He began to shake his head, meaning you will not do it. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abu Al-Rabi’ Al-Zahrani told us, Hammad ibn Zayd told us, Ayoub told us on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr that whenever the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) stopped at a place, he would not leave until he prayed there. When the Battle of Tabuk took place, he heard that Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul had said: The more honorable will expel the more humble from it. So he left before stopping at the end of the day. It was said to Abdul God ibn Ubayy said: Go to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) so that he may seek forgiveness for you. So God revealed: “When the hypocrites come to you, they say, ‘We bear witness that you are the Messenger of God.’ And God knows that you are His Messenger, and God bears witness that the hypocrites are liars. They have taken their oaths as a shield and averted [people] from the way of God. Evil indeed is that which they have been doing. That is because they believed and then disbelieved, so their hearts were sealed, so they do not understand. And when you see them, their bodies impress you, and when they speak, you listen to their speech. They are as if they were propped up pieces of wood. They think that every shout is against them. They are the enemy, so beware of them. May God destroy them! How are they deluded? And when it is said to them, ‘Come, that the Messenger of God may ask forgiveness for you,’ they turn their heads away.” This is a sound chain of transmission going back to Sa’id ibn Jubayr. His statement that this was during the Battle of Tabuk is questionable, rather it is not good, because Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul was not among those who went out on the Battle of Tabuk, but rather he returned with a group of the army. Rather, what is well-known among the authors of military expeditions and biographies is that this was during the Battle of Al-Murays’i’, which is the Battle of Banu Al-Mustaliq. Yunus bin Bakir said on the authority of Ibn Ishaq: Muhammad bin Yahya bin Hibban, Abdullah bin Abi Bakr, and Asim bin Umar bin Qatada told me in the story of Banu al-Mustaliq, that while the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was staying there, Jahjah bin Saeed al-Ghifari, who was a servant of Umar bin al-Khattab, and Sinan bin Wabar fought over water. Ibn Ishaq said: Muhammad bin Yahya bin Hibban told me: They crowded together over water and fought. Sinan said: O group of Ansar, and Jahjah said: O group of Muhajireen, and Zaid bin Arqam and a group of Ansar were with Abdullah bin Ubayy, and when he heard it he said: They have revolted against us in our country, and by God, we and these Quraysh robes are nothing but what the one who said: Fatten your dog and it will eat you, and by God, if we return to Medina, the more honorable will expel from it the more abject. Then he turned to those of his people who were with him and said: What have you done to yourselves? You have made them your country and shared your wealth with them. By God, if you had refrained from… Zaid bin Arqam may God be pleased with him heard it and went with it to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) while he was a young boy in the household of Umar bin Al-Khattab may God be pleased with him and told him the story. Umar may God be pleased with him said: O Messenger of God, order Ibad bin Bishr to have his head struck off. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: What will happen when people say, O Umar, that Muhammad kills his companions? No, but call out, O Umar, to leave. When Abdullah bin Ubayy heard that this had reached the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), he came to him and apologized to him, and swore by God that he had not said what Zaid bin Arqam had said. He was in a good place with his people and they said: O Messenger of God, perhaps this young boy was mistaken and what the man said was not proven. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) set out during a time when he usually did not set out. He was met by Usaid ibn Hudayr may God be pleased with him. He greeted him with the greeting of the Prophet and then said: By God, you have set out at a strange time when you do not usually set out. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Have you not heard what your companion Ibn Ubayy said? He claimed that when he comes to Madinah, the more honorable will expel from it the more humble. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: So you, O Messenger of God, are the honorable one and he is the humble one. Then he said: Be gentle with him, O Messenger of God, for by God, God brought you while we were stringing beads for him to go out, and he thinks that you have taken away his kingdom. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) set out with the people until evening, and the whole night until morning, and the beginning of the day until the sun had risen. Then he descended with the people to distract them from what he was talking about. The people were not safe from feeling the touch of the ground, so they slept, and Surah Al-Munafiqun was revealed. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bayhaqi said: Abu Abdullah Al-Hafiz told us, Abu Bakr bin Ishaq told us, Bishr bin Musa told us, Al-Hamidi told us, Sufyan told us, Umar bin Dinar told us, I heard Jabir bin Abdullah say: We were with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in a military campaign, and a man from the Muhajireen kicked a man from the Ansar. The Ansari said: O Ansar! And the Muhajireen said: O Muhajireen! So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: What is this call to ignorance? Leave it, for it is rotten. Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul said: They did it, and by God, if we return to Medina, the more honorable will expel the more humiliated from it. Jabir said: The Ansar were more numerous in Medina than the Muhajireen when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, arrived, then the Muhajireen increased in number after that, so Umar said: Let me strike off the head of this hypocrite. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Leave him, lest people say that Muhammad kills his companions. Imam Ahmad narrated it on the authority of Husayn bin Muhammad al-Marwazi on the authority of Sufyan bin Uyaynah, and al-Bukhari narrated it on the authority of al-Hamidi and Muslim on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah and others on the authority of Sufyan with a similar chain of transmission. Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us, Shu`bah told us, on the authority of al-Hakam, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka`b al-Qurazi, on the authority of Zayd ibn Arqam, who said: I was with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, during the Battle of Tabuk, and Abdullah ibn Ubayy said: If we return to Medina, the more honorable will expel the more humble from it. He said: So I came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and informed him. He said: Abdullah ibn Ubayy swore that none of that had happened. He said: My people blamed me and said: What did you want with this? He said: So I went and slept gloomy and sad. He said: Then the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent for me and said: God has accepted your excuse and confirmed your truth. He said: Then this verse was revealed: “They are the ones who say, ‘Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of God until they disperse.’ And to God belong the treasures of the heavens and the earth, but the hypocrites do not understand. They say, ‘If we return to Medina, the more honorable will surely expel therefrom the more humble.’” Al-Bukhari narrated it at this verse on the authority of Adam bin Abi Iyas on the authority of Shu’bah, then he said: Ibn Abi Za’idah said on the authority of Al-A’mash on the authority of Amr on the authority of Ibn Abi Layla on the authority of Zayd on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Tirmidhi and Al-Nasa’i also narrated it at this verse on the authority of Shu’bah on his authority. Another chain of transmission on the authority of Zayd Imam Ahmad, may God have mercy on him, said: Yahya bin Adam and Yahya bin Abi Bakir told us: Israel told us on the authority of Abu Ishaq, who said: I heard Zayd bin Arqam, and Ibn Abi Bakir said on the authority of Zayd bin Arqam, who said: I went out with my uncle on a military expedition and I heard Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul saying to his companions: Do not spend on those with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and if we return to Madinah, the more honorable will expel the more humble from it. So I mentioned that to my uncle, and my uncle mentioned it to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent for me, and I told him. So he sent for Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul and his companions, and they swore by God that they had not said anything. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called me a liar and he believed him, and I was afflicted with a worry the like of which I had never been afflicted with before. I sat in the house, and my uncle said: I only wanted the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to call you a liar and hate you! He said: Until God revealed, When the hypocrites come to you, He said: So the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) sent for me and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) recited it to me and then said: God has confirmed what you say. Then Ahmad also said: Hasan bin Musa told us, Zuhair told us, Abu Ishaq told us that he heard Zaid bin Arqam say: We went out with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) on a journey and hardship befell the people. Abdullah bin Ubayy said to his companions: Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) until they disperse from around him. He said: If we return to Madinah, the more honorable will expel therefrom the more humble. So I came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and informed him of that. He sent for Abdullah bin Ubayy and asked him, and he swore an oath as to what he should do. They said: Zaid lied, O Messenger of God. I was impressed by what they said, so God revealed my confirmation, When the hypocrites come to you, He said: And the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) called them and asked forgiveness for them, but they turned their heads. And the Almighty said: As if they were propped up pieces of wood. He said: They were men of the most beautiful kind. Al-Bukhari, Muslim, and Al-Nasa’i narrated it from the hadith of Zuhair. Al-Bukhari also narrated it, and Al-Tirmidhi from the hadith of Israel, both of them on the authority of Abu Ishaq Amr bin Abdullah Al-Subai’i Al-Hamadani Al-Kufi on the authority of Zaid with it. Another chain of transmission on the authority of Zayd Abu Isa al-Tirmidhi said: Abd ibn Humayd told us, Ubayd God ibn Musa told us, on the authority of Isra’il, on the authority of al-Suddi, on the authority of Abu Sa’id al-Azdi, who said: Zayd ibn Arqam told us: We went on an expedition with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and there were some Bedouins with us. We would race to the water, and the Bedouins would get to it before us. A Bedouin raced his companions to fill the basin, placing stones around it and putting a mat on it until his companions came. He said: Then a man from the Ansar came to the Bedouin and let go of the reins of his camel so that she could drink, but he refused to let go, so he grabbed a stone and the water subsided. The Bedouin raised his stick and struck the Ansari on the head with it, wounding him. Then Abdullah ibn Ubayy, the head of the hypocrites, came and informed him, and he was one of his companions. Abdullah ibn Ubayy became angry and said: Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of God until they disperse from around him, meaning the Bedouins. They used to attend the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he was eating. Then Abdullah said to his companions: When they disperse from Muhammad Bring Muhammad food so he and those with him can eat. Then he said to his companions: If you return to Medina, let the more honorable expel the more humble. Zaid said: I was riding behind my uncle. I heard Abdullah ibn Ubayy say what he said, so I informed my uncle. He went and informed the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) sent for him, and he swore an oath and denied it. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) believed him and called me a liar. My uncle came to me and said: I only wanted the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) to hate you and for the Muslims to call you a liar. I was overcome by such grief as had never befallen anyone before. While I was traveling with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) on a journey, and my head was heavy with worry, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came to me, stroked my ear, and smiled in my face. I would not have liked to have eternal life because of it. Then Abu Bakr caught up with me and said: What did the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say to you? I said: He did not say anything except that he stroked my ear and smiled in my face. He said: Be of good cheer. Then Umar caught up with me, and I said to him the same as I had said to Abu Bakr. When morning came, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) recited Surat al-Munafiqun. Al-Tirmidhi was the only one to transmit it and said: This is a good and authentic hadith. Al-Hafiz Al-Bayhaqi narrated it in this way on the authority of Al-Hakim on the authority of Abu Al-Abbas Muhammad ibn Ahmad Al-Mahboubi on the authority of Saeed ibn Masoud on the authority of Ubaidullah ibn Musa with it, and he added after the words of Surat al-Munafiqun 63:When the hypocrites come to you, they say, ‘We bear witness that you are the Messenger of God,’ until he reached They are the ones who say, ‘Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of God until they disperse,’ until he reached The more honorable will surely expel therefrom the more humble. Abdullah bin Lahi’ah narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Aswad Urwah bin Al-Zubayr in Al-Maghāzī, and Musa bin Uqbah also mentioned this story in this context in his Magāzī, but they made the one who conveyed the words of Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was Aws bin Arqam from Banu Al-Harith bin Al-Khazraj, so perhaps it was another conveyor or a misprint due to hearing, and God knows best. Ibn Abi Hatim, may God have mercy on him, said: Muhammad bin Aziz al-Ayli told us, Salamah told me, Aqil told me, Muhammad bin Muslim told me that Urwah bin al-Zubayr and Amr bin Thabit al-Ansari told him that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, led the expedition of al-Marisi’, in which the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, demolished the tyrant Manat, which was between the back of the paralyzed man and the sea. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent Khalid bin al-Walid, who defeated Manat. Two men fought in that expedition of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, one of them was from the Muhajireen and the other from Buhaiz, and they were allies of the Ansar. The man from the Muhajireen gained the upper hand over al-Buhaiz, so al-Buhaiz said: O group of Ansar, so some men from the Ansar supported him. The Muhajireen said: O group of Muhajireen, so some men from the Muhajireen supported him until there was some fighting between those men from the Muhajireen and the men from the Ansar, then a barrier was established between them, and every hypocrite or man in whose heart there was sickness withdrew to Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul, who said: You had hoped and been repelled, but now you are neither harming nor… It is useful, the jalabiyas have joined forces against us and they were calling every hadith of the migration jalabiyas, so Abdullah bin Ubayy, the enemy of God, said: By God, if we return to Medina, the more honorable will expel the more humiliated from it. Malik ibn Ad-Dukhshan, who was one of the hypocrites, said: Did I not tell you not to spend on those who are with the Messenger of God until they disperse? Umar ibn Al-Khattab heard of that, so he walked until he came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: O Messenger of God, give me permission to strike off this man who has led people astray. He meant Umar Abdullah ibn Ubayy. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to Umar: Or will you fight him if I order you to kill him? Umar said: Yes, by God, if you order me to kill him, I will strike off his head. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Sit down. Then Asid ibn Hudayr, who was one of the Ansar and then one of Banu Abd Al-Ashhal, came until he came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: O Messenger of God, give me permission to strike off this man who has led people astray. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Or will you fight him if I order you to kill him? He said: Yes, by God, if you order me to kill him, I will strike with the sword under his earring. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Sit down. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Give permission to depart. So he set out with the people and traveled that day, night, and the next day until the day was over. Then he dismounted and set out with the people for the same amount of time until he arrived in Medina in the morning, in three days, which he traveled from the back of the paralyzed. When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) arrived in Medina, he sent for Umar and summoned him. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to him, Which Umar would you have killed if I had ordered you to kill him? Umar said, Yes. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, “By God, if I had killed him that day, I would have humiliated men who, if I ordered them today to kill him, would have obeyed, and people would say that I attacked my companions and killed them patiently.” Then God, the Almighty, revealed, “They are the ones who say, ‘Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of God until they disperse.’ But to God belong the treasures of the heavens and the earth, but the hypocrites do not understand. They say, ‘If we return to Medina,’” 10:17. This is a strange context and it contains precious things that are not found anywhere else. Muhammad bin Ishaq bin Yasar said: Asim bin Omar bin Qatada told me that when Abdullah bin Abdullah bin Ubayy heard what had happened to his father, he came to the Messenger of God and said: O Messenger of God, I have heard that you want to kill Abdullah bin Ubayy because of what you have heard about him. If you are going to do it, then order me to do it and I will bring you his head. By God, the Khazraj know that they have never had a man more dutiful to his father than me. I fear that you will order someone other than me to kill him, but my soul will not allow me to see the killer of Abdullah bin Ubayy walking among the people and I kill him, thus killing a believer for an unbeliever and entering Hell. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Rather, we will be gentle with him and treat him well as long as he remains with us. Ikrimah, Ibn Zayd and others mentioned that when the people returned to Madinah, Abdullah ibn Abdullah stood at the gate of Madinah and drew his sword. People started passing by him. When his father, Abdullah ibn Ubayy, came, his son said to him: Behind you! He said: What is wrong with you, woe to you? He said: “By God, you will not pass from here until the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gives you permission, for he is the powerful one and you are the weak one.” When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came, and he was only walking in the rear, Abdullah ibn Ubayy complained to him about his son. His son Abdullah said: By God, O Messenger of God, he will not enter it until you give him permission. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave him permission. Abdullah said: “Now that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, has given you permission, then pass now.” Abu Bakr Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr Al-Hamidi said in his Musnad: Sufyan bin Uyaynah told us, Abu Harun Al-Madani told us: Abdullah bin Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul said to his father: By God, you will never enter Madinah until you say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is the most honorable and I am the most humiliated. He said: He came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, I have heard that you want to kill my father. By Him who sent you with the truth, I have never looked at his face out of awe of him. If you wish me to bring you his head, I will come to you, for I hate to see my father’s killer.
63:9: The Almighty says, commanding His believing servants to remember Him often, and forbidding them to let wealth and children distract them from that, and informing them that whoever is distracted by the pleasures and adornments of this worldly life from the obedience and remembrance of his Lord, then he is one of the losers who will lose themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection. Then He urged them to spend in His obedience, saying: And spend from what We have provided for you before death comes to one of you and he says, ‘My Lord, if only You would delay me for a short term so I could give charity and be among the righteous.’ Every negligent person regrets when dying and asks for a longer period, even if it is just a little, to seek forgiveness and make up for what he missed, but it is impossible. What happened was and what is coming will come, and each according to his negligence. As for the disbelievers, as the Almighty said: “And warn the people of the Day when the punishment will come to them, and those who did wrong will say, ‘Our Lord, delay us for a short term so we may answer Your call and follow the messengers. Did you not swear before that there would be no demise for you?’” And the Almighty said: “Until, when death comes to one of them, he says, My Lord, send me back, that I may do righteousness in that which I left behind. No! It is only a word he says. And behind them is a barrier until the Day they are resurrected. Then the Most High said: “And God will not delay a soul when its term has come. And God is Acquainted with what you do.” That is, He does not give respite to anyone after their time has come. He is All-Knowing and All-Aware of who is truthful in his words and questions, and who, if he were to be brought before Him, would return to something worse than what he was in. For this reason the Most High said: And God is Acquainted with what you do. Abu Isa Al-Tirmidhi said: Abd bin Hamid narrated to us, Jaafar bin Awn narrated to us, Abu Janab Al-Kalbi narrated to us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak bin Muzahim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Whoever has wealth sufficient to perform Hajj to the House of his Lord, or on which Zakat is due, and he does not do so, should ask to be returned to his Lord at the time of death. A man said: O Ibn Abbas, fear God, for only the disbelievers ask to be returned to his Lord. He said: I will recite to you a verse from the Quran about that: “O you who have believed, let not your wealth or your children divert you from the remembrance of God. And whoever does that - then it is those who are the losers. And spend from what We have provided for you before death approaches one of you and he says, “My Lord, if only You would delay me for a short term so I could give charity and be among the righteous.” But God will not delay a soul when its term has come. And God is Acquainted with what you do.” He said: What necessitates Zakat? He said: If wealth reaches two hundred or more. He said: What necessitates Hajj? He said: Provisions and a camel. Then he said: Abd bin Hamid told us, Abd al-Razzaq told us, on the authority of al-Thawri, on the authority of Yahya bin Abi Hayya, who is Abu Janab al-Kalbi, on the authority of al-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in a similar manner. Then he said: Sufyan bin Uyaynah and others narrated it on the authority of Abu Janab, on the authority of al-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, from his own words, and this is more authentic. Abu Janab al-Kalbi was deemed weak. I said: The narration of Ad-Dahhak from Ibn Abbas has an interruption, and God knows best. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ibn Nufayl told us, Sulayman ibn Ata’ told us, on the authority of Muslimah Al-Juhani, on the authority of his uncle, meaning Abu Mushajiah ibn Rib’i, on the authority of Abu Ad-Darda’ may God be pleased with him, who said: We mentioned the extension of one’s lifespan to the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him), so he said: “God does not delay a soul when its appointed time has come. The extension of one’s lifespan is that God grants a servant righteous offspring who supplicate for him, and their supplications reach him in his grave.” End of the interpretation of Surat Al-Munafiqun. Praise and thanks be to God, and with Him comes success and protection.
63:10: The Almighty says, commanding His believing servants to remember Him often, and forbidding them to let wealth and children distract them from that, and informing them that whoever is distracted by the pleasures and adornments of this worldly life from the obedience and remembrance of his Lord, then he is one of the losers who will lose themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection. Then He urged them to spend in His obedience, saying: And spend from what We have provided for you before death comes to one of you and he says, ‘My Lord, if only You would delay me for a short term so I could give charity and be among the righteous.’ Every negligent person regrets when dying and asks for a longer period, even if it is just a little, to seek forgiveness and make up for what he missed, but it is impossible. What happened was and what is coming will come, and each according to his negligence. As for the disbelievers, as the Almighty said: “And warn the people of the Day when the punishment will come to them, and those who did wrong will say, ‘Our Lord, delay us for a short term so we may answer Your call and follow the messengers. Did you not swear before that there would be no demise for you?’” And the Almighty said: “Until, when death comes to one of them, he says, My Lord, send me back, that I may do righteousness in that which I left behind. No! It is only a word he says. And behind them is a barrier until the Day they are resurrected. Then the Most High said: “And God will not delay a soul when its term has come. And God is Acquainted with what you do.” That is, He does not give respite to anyone after their time has come. He is All-Knowing and All-Aware of who is truthful in his words and questions, and who, if he were to be brought before Him, would return to something worse than what he was in. For this reason the Most High said: And God is Acquainted with what you do. Abu Isa Al-Tirmidhi said: Abd bin Hamid narrated to us, Jaafar bin Awn narrated to us, Abu Janab Al-Kalbi narrated to us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak bin Muzahim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Whoever has wealth sufficient to perform Hajj to the House of his Lord, or on which Zakat is due, and he does not do so, should ask to be returned to his Lord at the time of death. A man said: O Ibn Abbas, fear God, for only the disbelievers ask to be returned to his Lord. He said: I will recite to you a verse from the Quran about that: “O you who have believed, let not your wealth or your children divert you from the remembrance of God. And whoever does that - then it is those who are the losers. And spend from what We have provided for you before death approaches one of you and he says, “My Lord, if only You would delay me for a short term so I could give charity and be among the righteous.” But God will not delay a soul when its term has come. And God is Acquainted with what you do.” He said: What necessitates Zakat? He said: If wealth reaches two hundred or more. He said: What necessitates Hajj? He said: Provisions and a camel. Then he said: Abd bin Hamid told us, Abd al-Razzaq told us, on the authority of al-Thawri, on the authority of Yahya bin Abi Hayya, who is Abu Janab al-Kalbi, on the authority of al-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in a similar manner. Then he said: Sufyan bin Uyaynah and others narrated it on the authority of Abu Janab, on the authority of al-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, from his own words, and this is more authentic. Abu Janab al-Kalbi was deemed weak. I said: The narration of Ad-Dahhak from Ibn Abbas has an interruption, and God knows best. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ibn Nufayl told us, Sulayman ibn Ata’ told us, on the authority of Muslimah Al-Juhani, on the authority of his uncle, meaning Abu Mushajiah ibn Rib’i, on the authority of Abu Ad-Darda’ may God be pleased with him, who said: We mentioned the extension of one’s lifespan to the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him), so he said: “God does not delay a soul when its appointed time has come. The extension of one’s lifespan is that God grants a servant righteous offspring who supplicate for him, and their supplications reach him in his grave.” End of the interpretation of Surat Al-Munafiqun. Praise and thanks be to God, and with Him comes success and protection.
